sourceInformation.source: Trauma Center: Second Opinion (Atlus, Wii, 2006); an original game inspired by it
sourceInformation.genre: Simulation (surgical action with visual-novel medical drama)
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person surgeon's-eye fixed close-up on a 3D operating field; talking-head close-ups and 3/4 wide shots in story scenes
sourceInformation.tech: Riftlight Pixel Engine 0.46.0 (three.js r186 WebGPU, Rapier), plain JavaScript ES modules, esbuild 0.28 single-file bundle, AI Hub session client 1.4.0 (protocol 1), Playwright 1.63 for tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine-native low-poly 3D rendered as pixel art; tissue painted at runtime on a dithered canvas texture; busts, hands, tools and figures built from primitives in code; Kenney furniture props recoloured
sourceInformation.animation: Engine animation: HERO_CLIPS compiled onto custom rigged figures, tweens and particles, plus procedural tool, bust (blinks, brows, mouth from voice syllables) and tissue animation
sourceInformation.audio: All music, sound effects and voices written in code: chiptune Song data, SoundDef effects, Animalese-style gibberish voices rendered from formant syllables at boot; no audio files; music defaults to 10 percent
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub session protocol v1, shared-world mode, 1 to 4 seats, the game's own card, host-run sim with keyframes and snapshots; no network outside a session; couch co-op for up to 4 on one screen
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Node tests of the sim, content lint, bot playthrough of the whole campaign, balance report, codec size checks, audio render checks, Chromium WebGPU browser checks (pad stub, mouse, attract, touch profile, co-op) and the AI Hub harness (5 scenarios); no subagents
sourceInformation.research: The plan's planner read the source's Wikipedia page, the hub's protocol and the engine kit and ran engine spikes; this build read the plan, the engine guide and the hub README and spiked canvas textures, kit packs and rig-compatible figures

testingFeedback: About 16: an unfinishable Dies Irae final cut, stale bot targets, a magnet snap loop, a pause menu that closed itself, a hub card crash on colour strings, a headless crash and comm text that overflowed the strip
4: the unfinishable Dies Irae final cut, the pause menu closing itself, the hub card crash that failed the harness, and a lifted-plate trap
The scripted bot playthrough of every operation and the whole campaign in Node: it found sim bugs in seconds and doubled as the balance report
The first blank-canvas screenshots and the pixel-width text lint, which only approximates the font
engineFeedback: The look pipeline: a canvas texture on a toon material becomes pixel art with outlines on only the tools and creatures, plus headless mode and the check tool
A little: a game needs a cameraTarget hook or start fails, the HUD has no alpha rect, and HUD text takes number colours but not hex strings
The pure-data surgery sim (tools, strains, bot, rewind), the tissue canvas painter, the menu and prompt toolkit and the gibberish voices
Keeping gameplay in the fixed step while UI reads input in update, and getting 3D busts into the HUD strip
HUD rects and text with alpha and wrapping, and a render-to-HUD helper for 3D portraits
promptFeedback: The plan: verified facts, exact numbers, a build order and a cut list made a huge scope tractable
Sixty-character lines versus a 342-pixel-wide HUD cannot both hold, and the plan suggests 3D busts in the comm strip which the HUD cannot draw
Fitting ten operations, five bosses, co-op, the hub, a bot and the whole shell into one medium-effort run without stubs
State which plan details are hard requirements, give a smaller minimum scope, and fix the line-width rule

aiHub.name: Trauma Cantina
aiHub.description: A surgical drama in pixel art: ten operations of precise instruments, a terrifying nurse and a man-made disease named Mercy, with couch and AI Hub co-op.
aiHub.controls: Stick/mouse moves the tool; R2/click uses it; right stick or 1-8 picks a tool; L2/Space gift; L1/Shift steady; Options/Esc pauses
